purpose: User-provided and independently researched GitHub profile design references. Qualitative editorial observations, not an assessment of a person's identity, job readiness or accomplishments.

policy.defaultDesign: professional clarity, real work and restrained formatting
policy.expressiveDesign: allowed when images/typography explain the actual work; never add decoration for its own sake
policy.sourceLabels: user-supplied screenshots vs independently researched examples
policy.trendingCaveat: Trending measures attention, not the professionalism of a README. The requested GitHub monthly developer filter was not directly accessible; do not mislabel these profiles as verified monthly ranked developers.
policy.futureAdditions: Append one bounded entry per verified profile README. Re-review if a profile changes.

favorablePatterns: Code-like self-description as an original composition
One distinct visual identity where it supports the work
avoidCopying: Imitating another person's avatar, tarot art or biography
Followers, views and multiple decorative counters as hiring evidence

favorablePatterns: Concise specialization and personal technical interests
Direct links to actual research, projects and teaching
avoidCopying: Copying technical credentials or organization roles
Assuming a sparse page works without inspectable work

favorablePatterns: Single consistent visual motif instead of competing widgets
A coherent theme with a quiet layout
avoidCopying: A large illustration as a substitute for inspectable projects
Using another person's image without the necessary rights

favorablePatterns: One clear sentence about current work
Letting repository pins supply most of the evidence
avoidCopying: Treating trend badges as hiring proof
Copying the person's short introduction verbatim

favorablePatterns: A handful of purpose-labelled links
Using native GitHub pinned projects rather than duplicated cards
avoidCopying: Assuming link-only profiles suit a new candidate without strong work links
Publishing unrelated personal details by default

favorablePatterns: Brief research narrative followed by specific project descriptions
Concrete public work and cross-project contributions
avoidCopying: Replicating a long project inventory in a hiring-focused README
Repeating stars counters beside every project

favorablePatterns: A single personal visual can create a memorable identity
avoidCopying: An oversized GIF as the only hiring evidence
Motion or humor that obscures actual software work

favorablePatterns: Original domain-relevant illustrations that explain research
Purposeful diagram-to-project-to-evidence hierarchy
Consistent colors, typography and section hierarchy
avoidCopying: Assuming all candidates should reproduce a long illustrated site
Copying original artwork or attributing external metrics without checks

favorablePatterns: Extremely concise positioning with most credibility coming from native pinned repositories
avoidCopying: Copying a near-empty README when a lesser-known applicant needs to explain their work
Equating fame or popularity with content quality

favorablePatterns: Current work and releases surfaced through dated, practical links
Automated updates with clear ownership and freshness
avoidCopying: Copying frequent-update sections without a real maintenance workflow
Adding multiple dynamic feeds unrelated to the user's target role

favorablePatterns: Consistent terminal/Rust visual identity tied to actual tools
Theme-aware imagery that has genuine project relevance
avoidCopying: Assuming every developer benefits from numerous visual elements and badges
Copying assets or logos without rights and attribution

favorablePatterns: First-person narrative that connects a person's background to concrete projects
Outcome-oriented links with a recognizable voice
avoidCopying: Replicating unverified business claims from another profile
Automatically recommending large widget sections and activity images

favorablePatterns: Readme concise; inspect how the author relies on native GitHub project links
Text-first communication without a wall of decorative images
avoidCopying: Never copy the subject's wording, employer claims or identity
Do not equate individual popularity or engineering reputation with README design quality
